messages.subject: [statnet_help] Error when running ergm
messages.body_plain:
I am running an ergm on a large dataset from which I have sampled  
about 200 nodes (using the random walk approach suggested by Leskovec  
& Faloutsos 2006, Samplying from large graphs.)

I've tried the following:

Anet <- ergm(net ~ edges + edgecov(GD))

Anet <- ergm(net ~ edges + triangle)

Anet <- ergm(net ~ edges + triangle + transitive)


These three run fine, but the following both produce the same error:


Anet <- ergm(net ~ edges + triangle + edgecov(GD))

Anet <- ergm(net ~ edges + transitive + edgecov(GD))

Error in if (order) coefs[order, seq_len(order)] else numeric() :
   argument is not interpretable as logical
In addition: Warning message:
In if (order) coefs[order, seq_len(order)] else numeric() :
   the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used


Does anyone know what might be causing this please?

Thank you,

Thomas

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Error when running ergm
messages.body_plain:
Hi Thomas,

Once you have sampled the network, you need to let ergm know what has been 
observed, and what is known to be missing by design.  Othewise, ergm is 
expecting a completely observed network, and any unobserved ties are 
assumed to be "0".  Among other things, this will influence how you 
specify the GD edgecov matrix, since edgecov expects a square matrix.

The ergm and tergm tutorials have writeups of how to use egocentrically 
sampled data properly.  For adaptively sampled data, your best bet is this 
post from Mark Handcock to the statnet help list:

http://mailman2.u.washington.edu/pipermail/statnet_help/2009/000524.html

HTH,
Martina

messages.subject: [statnet_help] modeling asymmetric ties in statnet
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I would like to hear your advice on a problem I am encountering.

My research question is whether the ties boys (coded as 1) send to girls
(coded as 0) are more likely to be un-reciprocated than those girls send to
boys. I am taking three approaches.

1. Keep the full network and use nodemix. I think nodemix will count both
the number of un-reciprocated ties from boys to girls and mutual ties
between girls and boys to calculate (1, 0) ties. Similarly, it will count
both the number of un-reciprocated ties from girls to boys and mutual ties
between them to calculate (0, 1) ties. If we use the former as the
reference group, the number of mutual ties cancel out so that we can
interpret the coefficient for the latter as a relative tendency. Does this
make sense?

2. Keep only un-reciprocated ties in the network since we are interested in
only un-reciprocated ties. Still use nodemix. But I think statnet is not
built to model this type of network yet because there are no built-in
constrains controlling the uniform asymmetry yet.

3. I am not familiar with the term asymmetric. Suppose I estimate a model
like

model <- ergm ( SNet~ edges + asymmetric("boy", diff = TRUE) )

                   Estimate Std. Error MCMC %       p-value
edges            -4.2698526 0.02007895      0  0.000000e+00
asymmetric.boy.0 -1.3784407 0.04340871      0 4.499525e-221
asymmetric.boy.1 -0.9322624 0.05927340      0  9.998334e-56

How do I interpret asymmetric.boy.0 and asymmetric.boy.1?

One last question, is it possible to let nodemix vary by the types of ties
(symmetric vs. asymmetric)? It seems that some new terms need to be made to
address that.

Any help will be greatly appreciated. Many thanks!

best,

Weihua

-- 
Weihua (Edward) An

Assistant Professor of Sociology and Statistics
Indiana University Bloomington
752 Ballantine Hall
1020 East Kirkwood Avenue
Bloomington, IN 47405-7103
